children.name: Sesuvium ayresii Marais
children.description: Description. The description of S. ayresii was provided by Marais (1978). The most indicative characters of this species are small (up to 25 - 28 mm long, but usually smaller) terete or semi-terete leaves and (sub) Sesuvium sessile flowers (see Marais 1978, Hartmann 2002). Additionally, Marais (1978) reported a smaller number of stamens (12 - 20) that have never been observed in S. portulacastrum (stamens more than 30). The smaller seed size (~ 1 mm) of S. ayresii compared with S. portulacastrum

children.name: Sesuvium congense Welw. ex Oliv.
children.description: Erect to decumbent, perennial herb, often much-branched and with many flowers; taproot strong; bladder cells bulging, globose to slightly conical (the latter only on shoots), loose to dense cover of the surface of internodes, leaves and outside of flowers; internodes can be reddish and are usually rough from bladder cells when young, later becoming smooth and also lignifying slightly. Leaves short (∼ 10 mm long) and narrow-elliptic; very succulent with semi-terete cross section; usually appearin

children.name: Sesuvium crithmoides Welw.
children.description: Notes — C 4 species (Bohley et al. 2015). We do not know if Sesuoium crithmoides established a stable population in Georgia and still can be found there. Despite its distinct morphology with linear, terete leaves and large, red flowers, the species is not often found in collections. Sesuoium crithmoides and S. mesembryanthemoides appear to share the same habitat as well as sharing several traits that separate them from the other African Sesuoium species.

children.name: Sesuvium edmonstonei Hook.fil.
children.description: Sesuvium edmonstonei, commonly known as Galapagos carpet weed, is a species of plant in the family Aizoaceae.

children.name: Sesuvium humifusum  Bohley & G.Kadereit
children.description: Notes — Long petioles and tiny, greenish white flowers characterize this species. Annual C 4 species, glycophyte. No information on possible pollinators. Capable of self-pollination in the greenhouse. The description of morphological characters is mostly based on living material cultivated in the greenhouse. Due to its small size and the unequal tepals the perianth may appear 3 - parted at first sight.

children.name: Sesuvium hydaspicum  Gonç.
children.description: Procumbent annual herb, often much-branched; internodes pale or sometimes red and slender with a sparse cover of flat, hyaline bladder cells, sometimes particularly around the nodes. Leaves 10 – 20 mm long, elliptic to lanceolate, sometimes with retuse tips and sometimes slightly folded along midvein; petiolate. Bracts ∼ 1 mm long, lanceolate and translucent; one pair. Flowers (sub-) sessile, 5 – 10 mm long, pink or dark red. Stamens 5 – 7 or sometimes numerous. Ovary with 2 carpels and 2 styles

children.name: Sesuvium maritimum  Britton, Sterns & Poggenb.
children.description: Sesuvium maritimum is an annual herbaceous plant native to southeastern North America in the family Aizoaceae.

children.name: Sesuvium mezianum  Bohley & G.Kadereit
children.description: Creeping, perennial herb; shoots up to 0.4 m long, often rooting at nodes. Bladder cells not seen. Leaves obovate to oblanceolate 5 – 7 mm long, 2 – 3 mm wide; petioles short (1 – 3 mm); lateral flaps distinctly auriculate with entire margins. Flowers 3 – 5 mm long, (greenish-) white, pendant, pedicellate (pedicels 1 – 2 (– 3) mm). Stamens 3. Ovary with 3 carpels. Fruit a circumscissile capsule. Seeds not seen.

children.name: Sesuvium rubriflorum  Bohley & G.Kadereit
children.description: Procumbent herb with perennial root, root ca. 4 mm in diam; shape and size of bladder cells unknown. Leaves tiny (1 – 3 mm long); petiolate (1 – 2 mm long); lateral flaps colorless with fimbriate margins. Flowers ∼ 3.5 mm long, bright red; pedicel 3 – 7 mm long, very thin, almost hair-like. Stamens five. Ovary with 2 carpels and 2 short styles. Fruit an egg-shaped capsule, opening below middle. Seeds numerous, ∼ 0.2 mm long, brown.

children.name: Sesuvium sesuvioides  Verdc.
children.description: (Procumbent to) erect perennial herb or shrublet forming patches up to 1.5 m in diam and 40 cm in height; internodes terete and, at least when young, densely covered with bladder cells, sometimes also when older; shoots often much-branched and with a reddish or dark olive to grey color when dry. children.name: Drosanthemopsis bella Klak
children.description: Distribution and ecology: Drosanthemopsis bella is known from a single population near Garies in southern Namaqualand (Map 6). The plants grow in heavy loam over weathered shales in otherwise almost bare patches of quartz-gravel. Flowering takes place between August and September.

children.name: Drosanthemopsis diversifolia  Klak
children.description: Ecology and distribution: The species prefers deep loamy soils, with or without a thin cover of quartz gravel, in areas with winter rain, mean annual precipitation <125 mm. Flowering between July and September. The species is common in the Vanrhynsdorp and Vredendal districts and extends also to the north-east to the Calvinia district, where it is much rarer. Its most southern location is at the Doorn River Bridge, north of Clanwilliam (Fig. 6).

children.name: Drosanthemopsis kwaganapensis Klak
children.description: Conservation status: The species is known from two quartz patches between Port Nolloth and Grootmis. At both localities about 20 plants were seen. We propose an IUCN category of vulnerable (VU) in line with that for D. vaginata.
